steps.title: Set your compass
steps.content: Use a fixed compass: North is up, East right, South down and West left. A right turn changes direction clockwise; a left turn changes it anticlockwise.
steps.example: Facing North, a right turn means East. Facing East, a left turn means North.

steps.title: Track a turn
steps.prompt: A person faces North and turns right. Which direction are they facing?
steps.explanation: A clockwise quarter-turn from North points East.

steps.title: Track movement with coordinates
steps.content: Represent East as +x, West as −x, North as +y and South as −y. Add each movement to find the final position.
steps.example: 5 km North and 3 km East gives position (3,5). Straight-line distance from start is √(3²+5²) = √34 km.

steps.title: Find the final direction
steps.prompt: A person walks 4 km East, then 4 km North, then 4 km West. Where are they relative to the start?
steps.explanation: The east and west movements cancel. The person is 4 km North of the start.

steps.title: Find shortest distance
steps.content: For perpendicular movements, use the Pythagorean theorem: distance = √(horizontal² + vertical²). First cancel opposite movements on the same axis.
steps.example: 6 km East and 8 km North gives distance √(36+64) = 10 km.

questions.prompt: Facing West, a person turns left. Which way are they facing?
questions.explanation: A left turn from West points South.

questions.prompt: A person walks 5 km North and 5 km South. Where are they?

questions.explanation: Turning right from South points West.

questions.prompt: A person walks 2 km West and 6 km East. What is the net displacement?
questions.explanation: 6 km East − 2 km West = 4 km East.
